vision.title: Counting people is easy. Not counting the same person twice is the hard part.
vision.body: At church, a camera counts who walks in. YOLOv8 finds the people, ByteTrack follows each one across frames, and a count only happens when someone actually crosses the line. Stopped at the door and stepped back? Not counted again.

faq.q: How much does a system cost?
faq.a: It depends on scope. After our first call I send a fixed proposal with a set timeline and price.

faq.q: Do I need everything figured out before we talk?
faq.a: No. You just need to know the problem you want to solve; we'll design the scope together.

faq.q: Who owns the code and the data?
faq.a: You do. Code, database and credentials are handed over at the end of the project.

faq.q: Do you offer support after delivery?
faq.a: Yes. Fixes and improvements can be on demand or through a monthly plan.

faq.q: Do you work with clients outside Brazil?
faq.a: Yes. Everything works remotely, with video calls, in English or Portuguese.

about.title: About
story: I'm a fullstack developer from Toledo, in western Paraná, Brazil, with a degree in Science and Technology. I like taking a concrete problem, from a gym, a law firm or my church, and turning it into a system people use every day.

Today I work as an RPA developer {employerAt}, automating processes with Python and PHP. On the side I run Personal Manager, a gym SaaS that's in production, and I build websites and computer vision projects.
When I'm not coding, I'm behind a drum kit: I play at church and teach lessons. My faith and my family come before all of it, and they're the reason I take the work seriously.

how.title: Pragmatic decisions
how.body: I pick tools for the problem, not for the hype. Sometimes that's Firestore; sometimes it's PostgreSQL with Redis.

how.title: Complete delivery
how.body: Code, tests, deployment, docs and training. A system that only runs on my machine isn't delivered.

how.title: Docs for every audience
how.body: A README for developers, a manual for users and a summary for decision makers.

how.title: Local and cheap when it makes sense
how.body: The church people counter runs on a local computer with zero cloud cost. Not everything needs a paid server.
